claims: For the fixed hard pair, 0<KL(P0||P1)=O(log^4 n/n^4) and KL(P1||P0)=infinity.
Both-world dyadic tails, raw fourth moments, the localized score, a global reverse-log envelope and a good/bad-window split prove the bound.

results.title: Strengthened unconditioned reverse KL: log-squared bound
claims: For the same fixed pair, 0<KL(P0||P1)=O(log^2 n/n^4), while KL(P1||P0)=infinity.
An exact Poisson skyline posterior gives N|S=K+Poi(mD). The fixed-count/Poisson skyline density ratio is <3 on U<=1/2; the complement is separately superpolynomially controlled.

Poisson compensation identities, justified differentiation and restricted density comparison give E0(K-mU)^4=O(log^2 m). A verified weighted-tilt/conditional-variance identity gives the needed weighted L2 bound and E0 Q^2=O(log^2 m/m^4).

The inherited entropy architecture, including plus p_n singular mass, gives the strengthened reverse KL and E0 N=Omega_alpha(n^4/log^2 n) for started vectors; any finite uniform worst-case cap obeys the same lower order.
The inherited count-test upper bound O_alpha(n^4/log n) leaves one logarithmic factor between bounds.
limits: Only an upper bound on reverse information and lower bound on resource cost, not Theta, a matching logarithmic order, a lower information constant or an optimal test.
The fixed experiment never becomes Poisson; global constant-three density domination is false.
Source-guided specialized identities are proved from skyline densities. The prior-art sharper concentration is acknowledged but not needed in this proof.

Fresh vectors are independent of each other and common world-independent policy randomization. A vector is charged from its first observation, including incomplete, infinite or selectively retained query words.

A common measurable adaptive policy, fixed per-world error alpha in (0,1/2), and unconditional finite-stop-and-correct probability at least 1-alpha are required. Expected lower cost is under P0; a uniform worst-case cap is at least that expectation.

Poisson processes are proof auxiliaries only. The actual experiments stay fixed-count. Restricted density domination and a separately controlled bad-area event replace naive transfer of centered Poisson moment equalities.
